text: PostgreSQL reads eight settings. Credentials come environment, stay scripts version control. SQLite reads two. db path file, DBConnection_v9 creates first connect, along missing parent directory. six settings accepted ignored, configuration built environment variables still works. driver string matched case-insensitively SQLite: "sqlite", "SQLite" "SQLITE" select . "PostgreSQL Unicode" matched exactly, must equal entry odbcinst.ini.

previous_headings: What differs
what: Why the field types are closed
title: PostgreSQL and SQLite side by side
text: SQLite accepts declared type name. VARCHAR(100), TEXT(100) misspelling create table, affinity nobody asked warning. csdb therefore accepts six types rejects rest: DATE DATETIME declared types rather storage classes. DBConnection_v9 opens file extended_types = TRUE, reads back Date POSIXct. Without argument 2020-01-01 returns integer 18262.
code: csdb::DBTable_v9$new(   dbconfig = cfg_sqlite,   table_name = "cases",   field_types = c("location_code" = "VARCHAR(100)", "cases_n" = "INTEGER"),   keys = "location_code" )$create_table() # SQLite does not support the field type(s): location_code (VARCHAR(100)). # The supported types are: TEXT, INTEGER, DOUBLE, BOOLEAN, DATE, DATETIME.

previous_headings: What differs
what: Why the primary key cannot be added later
title: PostgreSQL and SQLite side by side
text: ALTER TABLE cases ADD CONSTRAINT ... PRIMARY KEY (...) near "CONSTRAINT": syntax error SQLite. key must therefore exist first CREATE TABLE. Two consequences follow. $upsert_data() needs key, CONFLICT (<keys>) requires matching PRIMARY KEY UNIQUE constraint. every delete path DELETE rather drop--rename, dropped key put back.

title: PostgreSQL and SQLite side by side
text: Use SQLite tests, examples, single-writer pipeline one machine. file: nothing install, nothing start, nothing authenticate . Use PostgreSQL one process writes, data outgrows one machine, row counts get large enough planner estimate honest answer exact COUNT(*) slow.

title: Introduction to csdb
text: csdb provides abstracted database-access layer Core Surveillance (csverse) ecosystem. package exposes two R6 classes: DBConnection_v9 — wraps single database connection manages lifecycle (connect, disconnect, reconnect). DBTable_v9 — represents one database table provides methods inserting, upserting, deleting rows, well managing indexes validating field types contents. Three backends supported. Microsoft SQL Server PostgreSQL connect ODBC read credentials environment variables, keeps credentials scripts version control. SQLite connects RSQLite, db file path server, port, user password read . vignette runs SQLite, file created tempfile(). Every chunk therefore executes machine database server. changes code pointed PostgreSQL instead, see vignette("backends", package = "csdb").

title: Introduction to csdb
text: DBConnection_v9$new() stores connection parameters open connection immediately. Calling $connect() opens connection; $disconnect() closes . $autoconnection field returns active connection, reconnecting automatically needed. example creates connection object, connects, inspects connection fields, disconnects. disconnecting, $connection reports DISCONNECTED, class() still reports driver type, reading $autoconnection opens file .

title: Introduction to csdb
text: DBTable_v9$new() takes dbconfig list (parameters DBConnection_v9), plus table_name, field_types, keys, indexes, validators. Keys define primary key used upsert operations. Validators can enforce field-type field-content constraints; validator_field_types_blank validator_field_contents_blank skip validation entirely. example creates table object backed SQLite file, clears existing rows, inserts bundled nor_covid19_cases_by_time_location dataset, connects, returns lazy tbl() reference via dbplyr. file new, $drop_all_rows() creates table index first reports removed 0 rows.
